newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles trade up nearly 15 pct - report.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles trade up nearly 15 pct - report.

text.p: International trade through Los Angeles soared nearly 15 percent to $124.2 billion during the first three quarters of 1996, according to a report released Monday.

Los Angeles remained the nation's busiest customs district, but the gap over New York narrowed. New York trade was up a solid 24.7 percent to $115.4 billion, according to the quarterly CMC-TradeWeek Regional Trade Report.
Detroit and San Francisco, third and fourth in volume, also posted strong increases in the first three quarters. Detroit trade was up nearly 14 percent to $96.9 billion.
San Francisco posted a nearly 20 percent increase to $79.8 billion in total trade, the report said.

Exports to Japan continued to fuel Los Angeles trade growth, jumping nearly 16 percent to $12.1 billion, while imports fell 4.1 percent to $21.6 billion. Trade with mainland China also grew swiftly, up nearly 21 percent to $15.1 billion, according to the report.

Top exports from Los Angeles included computer circuits and parts, aircraft, cotton, cars, and auto parts. Top imports included computers and parts, cars, telephone and office equipment, footwear and consumer electronics.
The CMC-TradeWeek Regional Trade Report is published by Claremont McKenna College and TradeWeek, a newsweekly covering international trade and finance.

The trade data were derived from import and export declarations filed by traders shipping goods through the Los Angeles customs district. The district includes the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach and Los Angeles International Airport.
